definition: GPT-5.6 (Generative Pre-trained Transformer 5.6) is a set of large language models (LLMs) developed by OpenAI and released on July 9, 2026.
details: It is a family of models that comes in three distinct variants, ranked from least to most capable: Luna, Terra, and Sol. The models were designed to expand user capabilities across enterprise work, coding, scientific research, and cybersecurity. Due to government restrictions levied by the Donald Trump administration, GPT-5.6 was first released as a limited preview only on June 26, 2026 for "small group of trusted partners", despite the planned public rollout in the same month. On August 10, 2026, GPT-5.6-Cyber was launched with Daybreak Blue and Red, and it solved and completed 95% of cybersecurity problems. On August 11, 2026, Astra now has "universal monitoring for risky actions and misalignment," with monitors watching over its "chain of thought" in order to stop the model if it starts to move into high risk activity.

explainer.lead: GPT-5.6 is OpenAI's family of large language models for enterprise work, coding, scientific research, and cybersecurity. Its three main variants offer increasing capability, while a separate cybersecurity version and Astra's monitoring system address specialized tasks and risky behavior.

tiers.eli5: GPT-5.6 is like a team of three computer helpers: Luna, Terra, and Sol, with each one more capable than the last. They can help with office work, programming, science, and computer security. A watcher called Astra checks for dangerous actions and can stop the helper before it goes too far.
tiers.practitioner: Practitioners can select Luna, Terra, or Sol according to the capability needed for enterprise, coding, research, or cybersecurity work. GPT-5.6-Cyber, launched with Daybreak Blue and Red, is the cybersecurity-focused option and completed 95% of cybersecurity problems. For high-risk deployments, Astra monitors risky actions, misalignment, and the model's chain of thought, stopping activity that crosses into high risk.
tiers.paperLevel: GPT-5.6 = {Luna, Terra, Sol}, with capability ordered Luna < Terra < Sol; it is an OpenAI LLM family released on July 9, 2026. GPT-5.6-Cyber extends the family for cybersecurity and is reported to have solved and completed 95% of cybersecurity problems. Astra adds universal monitoring for risky actions and misalignment, including intervention based on chain-of-thought monitoring.

flow: A user submits an enterprise, coding, scientific-research, or cybersecurity task.
The task is handled by Luna, Terra, or Sol according to the capability required; cybersecurity work can use GPT-5.6-Cyber.
Astra watches for risky actions and misalignment, including warning signs in the model's chain of thought.
The system stops high-risk activity; otherwise, the model completes its response.
explainer.origin: OpenAI developed GPT-5.6 and released it on July 9, 2026. Government restrictions from the Donald Trump administration led to an earlier limited preview on June 26, 2026, for a small group of trusted partners instead of the planned public rollout that month.
explainer.lineage: Within the family, Luna, Terra, and Sol form a progression from least to most capable. GPT-5.6-Cyber followed on August 10, 2026, and Astra's universal monitoring for risky actions and misalignment was described on August 11.
explainer.whyItMatters: The family applies one model line to several demanding kinds of work while offering different capability levels. Its cybersecurity variant and Astra's intervention mechanism also make security tasks and control of high-risk behavior central concerns.
